precepts.text: Nehemiah discerned the man urging him to hide in the temple was hired that he should be afraid, and do so, and sin; a leader who becomes afraid of what the heathen threaten is in the midst of sin, so if you carry a fearful spirit, repent.
precepts.point: Have not I commanded thee: not being afraid is a commandment. Fear does not come from the Most High; the only fear he deals with is fearing him and the judgments you suffer for disobeying him. Being scared of what man can do to you is a spirit from the devil, not from God.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
Nehemiah discerned the man urging him to hide in the temple: “Therefore was he hired, that I should be afraid, and do so, and sin, and that they might have matter for an evil report, that they might reproach me.”

He was hired that Nehemiah should be afraid, and do so, and sin. A leader who becomes afraid of what the heathen threaten is in the midst of sin. That is why the Lord commanded Joshua, “be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed”: fear leads a leader into sin and gives the enemy matter for an evil report. So if you carry a fearful spirit, repent.

precepts.text: Shemaiah counseled Nehemiah to hide in the temple because they will come to slay thee; Nehemiah answered, Should such a man as I flee? He was the governor the Most High set up for everybody to look up to, and he would not go in.
precepts.point: Nehemiah shows the right spirit. In the Persian captivity he had liberty from the king to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem, and the enemies Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem plotted to scare him off the work. A hired man urged him to hide in the temple because they were coming to slay him, and Nehemiah refused; operating in the spirit of fear is sin according to the scripture.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

precepts.why:
The Philistines came up with “thirty thousand chariots, and six thousand horsemen, and people as the sand which is on the sea shore in multitude”, far deeper than the three thousand Israel had prepared. The men of Israel saw they were in a strait and hid themselves “in caves, and in thickets, and in rocks, and in high places, and in pits.” The sons of God, the mighty men of valor, saw the enemy coming and started hiding, though the Lord had just defeated the Philistines for Israel in chapter 7.

Nehemiah shows the right spirit. In the Persian captivity he had liberty from the king to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem, and the enemies Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem plotted to scare him off the work. Shemaiah counseled him to hide: “Let us meet together in the house of God, within the temple, and let us shut the doors of the temple: for they will come to slay thee; yea, in the night will they come to slay thee.”

Nehemiah answered, “Should such a man as I flee? and who is there, that, being as I am, would go into the temple to save his life? I will not go in.” He was the governor the Most High set up for everybody to look up to, and he would not go in.

precepts.text: Nehemiah perceived that God had not sent him, but that Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him, that he should be afraid, and do so, and sin, and that they might have matter for an evil report to reproach him; fear in the leader would let the enemy call him weak and unfit to lead.
precepts.point: Nehemiah shows the right spirit. In the Persian captivity he had liberty from the king to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem, and the enemies Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem plotted to scare him off the work. A hired man urged him to hide in the temple because they were coming to slay him, and Nehemiah refused; operating in the spirit of fear is sin according to the scripture.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

precepts.why:
Nehemiah saw through it: “And, lo, I perceived that God had not sent him; but that he pronounced this prophecy against me: for Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.” And he names the purpose: “Therefore was he hired, that I should be afraid, and do so, and sin, and that they might have matter for an evil report, that they might reproach me.”

Afraid, and do so, and sin: operating in the spirit of fear is sin according to the scripture. Fear in the leader would let the enemy call him weak and unfit to lead. Israel did what Nehemiah refused to do; they hid, and the people that stayed with Saul “followed him trembling.”

note.label: The Religious Peer Pressure of Fred Price Jr

points: Then Nehemiah perceived that God had not sent him: Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him. The heathen hired one of his own people to convince the leader to run and hide, so they could have matter for an evil report and reproach him. He sold his people out.

note.label: The Religious Peer Pressure of Fred Price Jr

points: Shemaiah urged Nehemiah to hide in the temple, but he had been hired by Tobiah and Sanballat to make Nehemiah afraid and give them matter for an evil report.
Should such a man as I flee? Leaders will be targeted by brethren paid to defame them.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

points: When Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arabian, and the rest of the enemies hear that the wall is built with no breach left, though the doors are not yet set on the gates, they turn to another plan.
With the wall standing, the enemies shift from open threat to schemes against Nehemiah himself.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: Sanballat and Geshem send for Nehemiah to meet together in one of the villages in the plain of Ono, but they think to do him mischief.
The invitation is a trap to draw Nehemiah away and harm him.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: Nehemiah sends messengers saying he is doing a great work and cannot come down, asking why the work should cease while he leaves it to come to them.
Nehemiah uses wisdom, refusing to leave the work for a meeting he knows is a plot to put him to death.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: They send to him four times after the same manner, and he answers them the same way each time.
The enemies keep pressing, and Nehemiah keeps giving the same steady refusal.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: The fifth time Sanballat sends his servant with an open letter in his hand.
The open letter is meant to be read by others, a public pressure tactic against Nehemiah.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: The letter reports among the heathen, and Geshem says it, that Nehemiah and the Jews think to rebel and that this is why he builds the wall, that he may be their king.
The enemies invent a charge of rebellion to frighten Nehemiah and give the king cause against him.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: The letter claims Nehemiah has appointed prophets to proclaim him king in Judah and threatens to report it to the king, inviting him to take counsel together.
The false report is designed to force Nehemiah into their meeting under fear.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: Nehemiah answers that there are no such things done as they say, but that they feign them out of their own heart.
Nehemiah plainly names the accusation as an invention of their own minds.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: They all try to make the builders afraid, saying their hands shall be weakened so the work is not done, and Nehemiah prays for the Most High to strengthen his hands.
The whole aim is to weaken the hands and stop the work, so Nehemiah turns to the Most High for strength.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: Shemaiah, shut up in his house, tells Nehemiah to meet within the temple and shut the doors because men will come to slay him in the night.
A hired man tries to lure Nehemiah into hiding in the temple, framing it as safety.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: Nehemiah answers, should such a man as I flee, and who, being as I am, would go into the temple to save his life, and says he will not go in.
Nehemiah refuses to run or to misuse the temple to save himself, standing firm in his place.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: Nehemiah perceives that the Most High had not sent Shemaiah, but that Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him to pronounce this prophecy.
Nehemiah discerns the false prophecy and sees the hand of the enemies who paid for it.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: Shemaiah was hired so that Nehemiah would be afraid, do so, and sin, giving them matter for an evil report to reproach him.
The scheme is to trap Nehemiah into a fearful sin they could use to shame him.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: Nehemiah asks the Most High to think upon Tobiah, Sanballat, the prophetess Noadiah, and the rest of the prophets who would have put him in fear according to their works.
He commits the hired accusers and false prophets to the judgment of the Most High.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: The wall is finished on the twenty-fifth day of the month Elul, in fifty-two days.
Despite all the plots, the whole wall is completed in fifty-two days.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: When the enemies and all the heathen about them hear of it, they are much cast down in their own eyes, for they perceive that the work was wrought of the Most High.
The completed wall shames the enemies, who recognize that this was the work and pleasure of the Most High.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: In those days the nobles of Judah send many letters to Tobiah, and his letters come to them.
Even inside Judah some remain tied to Tobiah, keeping a line of communication with the enemy.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: Many in Judah are sworn to Tobiah because he is the son-in-law of Shechaniah and his son married the daughter of Meshullam.
Marriage alliances bind some of Judah to the enemy, dividing loyalty within the people.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots

points: They report Tobiah's good deeds before Nehemiah and carry Nehemiah's words to Tobiah, and Tobiah sends letters to put him in fear.

To the end the enemy uses those inside to pressure and frighten Nehemiah, the same way anything that can be done to stop the work of the Most High is still done today, and the people must keep their spiritual eyes open to see it.

note.label: Nehemiah 6: The Wall Finished Against the Enemies' Plots
